title: Scheduler: incorporate streaming + prompt-length buckets into batching heuristics
author: Marcus Reed
description:
Context: As part of workload-aware batching defaults (fast/standard/cost-efficient), we need the scheduler to treat streaming traffic and different prompt-length regimes differently. Today the continuous batching heuristics mostly infer load from queue depth and token estimates, but they do not explicitly model streaming vs non-streaming, and they assume a roughly unimodal prompt length distribution. This leads to poor trade-offs under mixed traffic (e.g., streaming chat requests getting stuck behind large-prefill summarization requests).

This PR introduces two lightweight workload signals into the scheduler decision inputs:
- streaming flag: whether the request is streaming (server-sent events / chunked) vs non-streaming
- prompt-length bucket: coarse bucketing based on prompt token count, used to steer wait budgets and batch formation

What changed:
- Add RequestWorkloadSignals { is_streaming, prompt_len_bucket } plumbed from request admission -> queue item -> batch builder.
- Define prompt length buckets (defaults): 0-256, 257-1024, 1025-4096, 4097+ tokens (names: XS/S/M/L). These are intentionally coarse to avoid high-cardinality telemetry and brittle tuning.
- Update batch builder heuristic to avoid mixing extreme buckets by default (e.g., L with XS) when it would inflate tail latency; mixing is still allowed under explicit overload mode / when queue pressure is high.
- Update wait-budget selection to bias streaming requests toward shorter max-wait and earlier decode start (does not change the tier defaults in this PR; it only adds the signals to enable follow-up tier tuning).
- Add unit tests covering: correct bucketing boundaries; stable behavior under mixed streaming/non-streaming; and regression tests for starvation (streaming XS requests should make progress even with a backlog of non-streaming L prefill).

Notes / non-goals:
- No per-tenant auto-tuning here; this is strictly feature plumbing + conservative heuristics.
- No new external config surface area in this PR.
- Telemetry changes are limited to internal debug counters; tier labels and reason codes come in later PRs.

Rollout: behind runtime flag scheduler.workload_signals.enabled (default: false). Follow-ups will enable this in canary once tiered defaults land.

Docs: none (internal behavior only).
commits: scheduler: add prompt length bucketing helper + constants
scheduler: plumb is_streaming and prompt_len_bucket through queue items
scheduler: batch builder uses workload signals to prefer compatible mixes
tests: add unit coverage for bucketing + mixed streaming scenarios
chore: add internal debug counters for signal distribution
test_plan:
1) Unit tests: runtime-scheduler test suite (added coverage for bucket boundaries and mixed traffic).
2) Local simulation: ran scheduler micro-sim with mixed workloads (streaming XS chat + non-streaming L summarization) and verified streaming p99 does not regress vs baseline when flag is enabled.
3) Safety: verified flag default remains false and no behavior change when disabled.
review_conversation:
Sofia Ivanova: Can we keep buckets coarse enough that we don’t end up tuning ourselves into a corner? Also worried about mixing rules causing throughput loss under normal traffic.
Marcus Reed (author): Agree. Buckets are XS/S/M/L with fixed boundaries and the mix policy is a preference not a hard constraint; under queue pressure we still mix. Added a test to ensure batching still happens under sustained load.

Omar El-Sayed: For streaming, we need to be explicit that the ‘shorter wait budget’ should not starve long prefill. Do we have fairness coverage?
Marcus Reed: Added a fairness regression test where a backlog of non-streaming L exists and streaming XS arrives continuously; both progress. The mix policy only biases candidate selection; queue admission/fairness remains unchanged.

Lena Fischer: Can you add comments on why we chose these boundaries? Also please avoid exporting bucket labels into metrics yet (cardinality risk).
Marcus Reed: Added rationale comments in workload_signals.rs and kept telemetry to debug counters only; no labels exported.

Noah Patel: The bucketing should use the same tokenizer/token estimate path we use elsewhere; otherwise boundaries drift.
Marcus Reed: Updated to use existing token estimate function from request_context; added a unit test that uses the same estimator.

Julian Moore: Please ensure the flag is wired through the config/feature flag layer so we can kill-switch it during canary.
Marcus Reed: Added scheduler.workload_signals.enabled gate in flags.rs and guarded heuristic changes behind it.

Final: Sofia approved after requested comments/tests were added. Omar approved with note to watch fast-tier p99 during canary once enabled.
release_notes: Internal-only: scheduler can optionally consider streaming + prompt-length buckets (feature-flagged). Enables follow-up workload-aware batching tier tuning.
